UnityPoint Health — St. Luke’s introduces new robotic microbiology system

By: John LohmanCBJ News Staff|August 3, 2026
|1 min read
  • Bookmark
    • You must be a subscriber to save articles. Subscribe Today!

    • BD Kiestra and St. Luke's team members. CREDIT UNITYPOINT

    Listen to audio version of this article
    Sponsored by
    0:00 / 1:00
    Instaread

    UnityPoint Health — St. Luke’s Hospital has introduced a new BD Kiestra Microbiology Automation system, an advanced robotic laboratory platform designed to enhance the efficiency, consistency, and quality of microbiology testing. This marks the second robotic laboratory automation system the organization has implemented.

    The BD Kiestra system automates numerous routine laboratory functions, including specimen processing, incubation, digital imaging, and culture workflows. By minimizing manual steps, the system establishes a more efficient and traceable laboratory process.

    “Automation allows our team to focus more on the complex, meaningful aspects of microbiology testing,” said Wendy Bienemann, executive director of laboratory services in a statement. “Our professionals can dedicate more attention to reviewing results, working on complex cases, and ensuring the highest level of quality.”

    The system also promotes a more standardized testing process across UnityPoint Health laboratories, while supporting future growth and rising testing volumes.

    “By modernizing our microbiology operations, we’re strengthening our ability to provide timely results that help clinicians make informed treatment decisions,” Ms. Bienemann added.
